deckTitle: Fractal Future Fantasy: The Wrinkle-Rumble Starter Kit

cards.power: Eavesdrop: Look at the top 3 cards of the deck. Groan loudly at what you see.
cards.lore: As the body fails, the sensors expand. You will hear every insult whispered by the youth.
cards.gradeReason: Groaning at cards is fun but only lands once you know what you peeked at.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: aged ink watercolor. Subject: elderly cat with enormous drooping nose eavesdropping on cards. Mood: suspicious decay.

cards.power: Swap Equipment: Steal an item from a player. Give them "Gingivitis" in return.
cards.lore: The indignity isn't losing your teeth; it's accidentally wearing your enemy's smile.
cards.gradeReason: Steal an item, hand back fake teeth — the indignity is mechanical and instant.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: splatter ink comic. Subject: dog and cat mid-teeth-swap chaos mid-run. Mood: gleeful dental horror.

cards.power: Collision: Destroy 1 Future Timeline card. Both players cry.
cards.lore: If you do not complete the mission, you age instantly. The diaper remains constant.
cards.gradeReason: Destroy a timeline card, both players cry — the mechanic makes you perform it.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: watercolor explosion. Subject: two elderly figures on scooters triggering mushroom cloud. Mood: inevitable catastrophe.

cards.power: Clog: Block a pathway. No one moves until you are surgically removed.
cards.lore: A diet of fast food leads to a legacy of posterior facial hair.
cards.gradeReason: Block a pathway until surgically removed — vivid, bodily, non-negotiable table moment.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: gross-out ink. Subject: badger wedged in red pipe surrounded by cascading posterior hair. Mood: undignified blockade.

cards.power: Misread: Interpret a Rule Card incorrectly on purpose. Opponents must prove you wrong.
cards.lore: The future is bright. Too bad you can't see it.
cards.gradeReason: Misreading a rule on purpose is great comedy — only works once the rulebook is shared.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: ink crosshatch. Subject: mole in thick goggles squinting at illegible document. Mood: willful confusion.

cards.power: Space Hog: Occupy two zones at once. Push others into the Void.
cards.lore: Push people away, and you grow old alone. And by alone, we mean "wide".
cards.gradeReason: Occupying two zones is clear as a mechanic but thin as a performance cue.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: watercolor celebration. Subject: rotund raccoon in birthday dress expanding outward at table. Mood: oblivious expansion.

cards.power: Camouflage: Fail a stealth check. Everyone knows it's a squirrel.
cards.lore: Graceful aging is a myth sold by hat salesmen.
cards.gradeReason: Failing stealth while obviously wearing a squirrel is funny — needs a stealth system to pop.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: ink comedy. Subject: eagle with live squirrel on head failing to look inconspicuous. Mood: transparent self-delusion.

cards.power: Rust: -5 to Agility. You can now predict rain with your joints.
cards.lore: The mind wants to tango. The cartilage wants to crumble.
cards.gradeReason: Predicting rain with joints is poetic, but -5 Agility needs a stat system to sting.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: loose watercolor. Subject: stork with creaking hinge-knees in windswept field, CREAK sound effects. Mood: structural failure.

cards.power: Stalemate: Skip your turn to ensure your opponent also skips theirs.
cards.lore: Seventy years later, we still haven't decided who gets the top bunk.
cards.gradeReason: Mutual turn-skip as relationship warfare is smart — needs both players invested to land.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: rough ink. Subject: two elderly possums screaming from bunk beds into eternity. Mood: entrenched stalemate.

cards.power: Inciting Incident: Restart the game from Turn 1. Keep all damage.
cards.lore: The war didn't start over land or ideology. It started over a snickerdoodle.
cards.gradeReason: Restart from Turn 1 keeping all damage — the most catastrophic snickerdoodle in history.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: cosmic horror watercolor. Subject: glowing cookie surrounded by green lightning vortex in void. Mood: apocalyptic pastry.

cards.power: Petty Theft: Steal one resource. Claim it was yours for 40 years.
cards.lore: Robots may inherit the earth, but they will still have to listen to us argue about condiments.
cards.gradeReason: Stealing a resource and claiming 40 years of ownership — needs a resource to steal.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: tense ink illustration. Subject: aardvark and rabbit arguing over Ranch bottle across barbed-wire table. Mood: condiment warfare.

cards.power: Regret: Take 10 Psychic Damage. Heal an opponent 10 HP.
cards.lore: He died hating you. You win the argument, but lose the soul.
cards.gradeReason: Taking damage to heal opponent is a beautiful mechanic — emotional weight needs setup.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: somber watercolor. Subject: furry hand clutching disintegrating letter near gravestone with flower. Mood: permanent regret.

cards.power: Filibuster: Talk uninterrupted for 60 seconds. If you stop, you lose.
cards.lore: We will dismantle the establishment, even if we are decomposing while doing it.
cards.gradeReason: Filibustering 60 seconds is instantly playable — naming a cause to dismantle amplifies it.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: protest cartoon watercolor. Subject: decaying squid holding UNFAIR sign next to SpongeBob in cobweb. Mood: absurdist resistance.

cards.power: Chivalry isn't dead, it's just on life support and very angry.
cards.lore: Joust: Roll a d6. On a 1, you have a heart attack. On a 6, opponent dies.
cards.gradeReason: Roll d6: heart attack or opponent dies. Pure chaos lever, zero ambiguity. Power/lore intentionally inverted.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: action watercolor. Subject: bear and rabbit in wheelchairs jousting with IV poles mid-spark. Mood: defiant geriatric glory.

cards.power: Entanglement: Bind yourself to another player. If you fall, they fall.
cards.lore: Hope is for people who aren't stuck in a tree for 70 years with Harold.
cards.gradeReason: Binding to another player so you fall together — physical commitment nobody can ignore.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: overgrown ink. Subject: two elderly men tangled in massive tree, football lodged in beard knot. Mood: grudge eternal.

cards.power: Recursion: Replay the last turn exactly as it happened. Blame the dice.
cards.lore: It's your fault. No, it's my fault. No, it's your fault for making it my fault.
cards.gradeReason: Replay last turn, blame the dice — ouroboros of accountability everyone recognizes instantly.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: fiery circle watercolor. Subject: ouroboros snake biting itself amid cursing symbols and flame. Mood: recursive fury.

cards.power: Hold Music: Force an opponent to hum a tune while you think. If they stop, they skip a turn.
cards.lore: Madame Foster is just finishing up. She's been in the craft aisle for three decades.
cards.gradeReason: Forcing humming as a delay tactic is funny — depends on opponent's commitment to the bit.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: vintage craft store horror. Subject: skeleton waiter in cobwebbed chair holding deli number ticket. Mood: indefinite waiting.

cards.power: Gravity Trap: You cannot leave this card until you roll a double.
cards.lore: The ride ends when you die. Please keep arms and legs inside the existential dread.
cards.gradeReason: Trapped until you roll doubles is tense — visual of the infinite slide sells the dread.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: watercolor spiral descent. Subject: tiny figure in striped tube slide descending into black void. Mood: existential theme park.

cards.power: Analysis Paralysis: Force a player to answer a trivia question. If they hesitate, they freeze.
cards.lore: If you win, you have to keep playing. The only winning move is to be wrong.
cards.gradeReason: Force trivia, hesitation means freeze — behavioral trigger lands at any table, immediately.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: game show watercolor. Subject: bespectacled aardvark at buzzer podium in full panic. Mood: analysis paralysis.

cards.power: Nonsense Call: Shout a random phrase. Any player who laughs takes damage.
cards.lore: I made a brother! He smells like feet and listens to my screams.
cards.gradeReason: Shout random phrase, laughers take damage — pure performance, zero setup required.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: slapstick ink. Subject: screaming yellow blob holding sock to ear against brick wall. Mood: infectious nonsense.

cards.power: Held Back: Negate a 'Level Up' card. You must repeat the tutorial.
cards.lore: There is always next year. And the year after that. Mr. Ratburn is immortal.
cards.gradeReason: Negating Level Up is mechanically fine but invites nothing to embody at the table.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: school watercolor. Subject: elderly rabbit hunched at child's desk surrounded by flying pink pigs. Mood: academic purgatory.

cards.power: Caution: Skip your turn to gain +1 Defense. Bore your opponents to death.
cards.lore: He never took a risk. His heart beat perfectly until the moment it died of boredom.
cards.gradeReason: Skip turn for defense until you die of boredom — the irony lands, mechanic is dry.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: graveyard watercolor. Subject: gravestone reading HE WAS CAREFUL amid lightning and scattered skulls. Mood: boring immortality.

cards.power: Procrastination: Push any negative effect to the next turn. Repeat indefinitely.
cards.lore: Art is 1% inspiration and 99% staring at a wall until you die.
cards.gradeReason: Push negative effects forward forever — procrastination as mechanics is self-evident satire.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: overgrown typewriter ink. Subject: vine-smothered typewriter with Chapter 1. half-typed in dusty light. Mood: creative paralysis.

cards.power: Validation: Gain 1 point for doing absolutely nothing.
cards.lore: You showed up. That was the extent of your contribution to history.
cards.gradeReason: Gain a point for nothing — the dusty urn as trophy is the entire philosophy in one image.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: dusty shelf watercolor. Subject: lonely funeral urn on cobwebbed shelf where a trophy should be. Mood: anticlimax.

cards.power: Automation: Replace your hand with a random algorithm (roll dice for actions).
cards.lore: The future is efficient. You are not. Please vacate the premises.
cards.gradeReason: Replacing your hand with dice rolls is interesting — displacement joke needs the robot visible.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: industrial watercolor. Subject: silver robot handing pink FIRED slip to crying dog construction worker. Mood: efficient ruthlessness.

cards.power: Tech Upgrade: +5 Attack, but you forget who you are attacking.
cards.lore: In the year 2000, the hunt doesn't require aim, just batteries.
cards.gradeReason: +5 attack but forget the target — funny dependency, needs attack rolls to fully sing.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: tech western watercolor. Subject: gruff pig in tweed jacket wielding laser cane firing into empty dirt. Mood: armed confusion.

cards.power: Payback: Reflect all damage taken in the early game back to the dealer.
cards.lore: The weak shall inherit the gym, and the gym teacher shall inherit the hernia.
cards.gradeReason: Early damage reflected back is satisfying — but 'early game' needs temporal game framing.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: gym class fury watercolor. Subject: ripped squirrel vs. old man struggling with giant tractor tire. Mood: delayed vengeance.

cards.power: Levitation: Immune to Ground attacks. Vulnerable to Dignity attacks. Science conquered gravity solely to deal with incontinence.
cards.gradeReason: Immune to Ground, vulnerable to Dignity — elegant immunity axis, but needs status system to shine.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: sci-fi domestic watercolor. Subject: glowing levitating diaper beside stoic duck retiree in bathrobe. Mood: gravity defeated.

cards.power: Scavenge: Draw cards from the discard pile. They smell bad.
cards.lore: When the nanny throws you out, you become King of the Dump.
cards.gradeReason: Scavenge from discard is clean — the smell joke is the hook but discard needs to be loaded.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: post-apocalyptic watercolor. Subject: troll king enthroned on garbage heap with rat court and fish-bone crown. Mood: sovereign filth.

cards.power: Isolation: You cannot be targeted by others. You also cannot win.
cards.lore: Happy 100th Birthday. Your only friend is a piece of dental wire.
cards.gradeReason: Untargetable but can't win is a brilliant paradox — needs opponents to feel the isolation.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: sad birthday watercolor. Subject: monkey alone at centennial party table with dental wire as only guest. Mood: isolated celebration.

cards.power: Institutionalize: Remove a character from play. They are 'safe' now.
cards.lore: A nice place where the soup is warm and the doors are locked from the outside.
cards.gradeReason: Remove character to safety with locked doors — cynicism reads but needs character removal rules.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: brutalist watercolor. Subject: grey concrete residential block descending into abyss void. Mood: institutional comfort.

cards.power: Drift: Move in a random direction every turn. Ignore physics.
cards.lore: Rocking back and forth is the only propulsion left.
cards.gradeReason: Rocking chair in space drifting randomly — perfect visual but grid movement needed.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: cosmic watercolor. Subject: rocking chair floating through starfield with trailing rope in silence. Mood: propulsion of despair.

cards.power: Judgment: Reveal your hand. If you have any "Stolen Items", lose the game.
cards.gradeReason: Moral accounting at the gate — needs the Stolen Items economy to exist in play.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: heavenly clouds watercolor. Subject: holy sheep at podium pointing GO AWAY at mouse with bouncy ball. Mood: divine audit.

cards.power: Nostalgia: Skip your turn to relive a better turn from the past.
cards.lore: The music stopped forty years ago, but the feet keep moving.
cards.gradeReason: Skip turn to relive better past — poignant but depends on remembering past turns.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: ghost watercolor. Subject: wolf couple dancing as blue ghosts in cobwebbed Victorian drawing room by clock. Mood: nostalgic haunting.

cards.power: Wake Up: Cancel all active "Future" effects. Return to reality.
cards.lore: It was all a dream. A terrible, wrinkly, arthritis-filled dream.
cards.gradeReason: Cancel all Future effects — needs Future effects active to be satisfying.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: dream-burst watercolor. Subject: sleeping figure under rubble of exploded dream cloud and debris. Mood: rude awakening.

cards.power: Meta-Strike: Drop a 16-ton weight on the Game Master.
cards.lore: When the plot gets too depressing, complain to the writers until they drop an anvil.
cards.gradeReason: Drop 16 tons on the Game Master — meta-attack on the fiction itself, zero setup needed.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: cartoon thunder. Subject: enormous red DO NOT TOUCH button hanging from storm clouds on rope. Mood: temptation incarnate.

cards.power: Effect: Block all 'Future' cards. If you can't see it, it isn't happening.
cards.lore: The ultimate defense against reality.
cards.gradeReason: Smiley-face helmet blocking Future cards is iconic — but Future card category needs to exist.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: armored comedy watercolor. Subject: knight helmet with yellow smiley face visor in soft diffused light. Mood: cheerful ignorance.

cards.power: Effect: Prevents a character from moving, changing, or growing as a person.
cards.lore: Why move forward when you can stay here and be angry?
cards.gradeReason: Preventing character growth is profound satire — mechanical dependency on character movement system.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: chains and rust watercolor. Subject: anchor embedded in earth, heavy chains wrapped around bear paw. Mood: voluntary stagnation.

cards.power: Effect: Force a 'Dream Sequence' turn skip on any player acting too energetic.
cards.lore: For when the young people are being too loud.
cards.gradeReason: Dream Sequence skip for loud players is behavioral fun — Dream Sequence needs to exist in rules.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: sleepy impact watercolor. Subject: ZZZZZT-engraved wooden hammer mid-swing with star bursts and sparks. Mood: enforced quiet time.

cards.power: Effect: Allows player to rewrite the text of one card with a marker.
cards.lore: Escape the medium.
cards.gradeReason: Rewrite a card's text with a marker — literal object becomes meta-weapon, no explanation needed.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: shattered glass ink. Subject: red brick crashing through card frame amid exploding glass shards. Mood: medium escape.

cards.power: Field Effect: All movement speed is halved. Bathroom breaks double.
cards.lore: Drink deep and feel your bones liquefy.
cards.gradeReason: Halve speed, double bathroom breaks — field effect needs movement rules but lore is instant.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: baroque decay watercolor. Subject: crumbling ornate fountain oozing purple liquid in empty garden. Mood: beautiful deterioration.

cards.power: Field Effect: Every step deals Psychic Damage based on past embarrassments.
cards.lore: Watch your step. That's where you called your teacher 'Mom'.
cards.gradeReason: Psychic damage from embarrassments — cringe is the mechanic, triggers immediately at any table.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: suburban horror watercolor. Subject: suburban sidewalk with labeled CRINGE mines exploding along path. Mood: weaponized nostalgia.

cards.power: Field Effect: Looking through it causes 'Depression' status.
cards.lore: Look at the life you could have had. Now look at your hand. Cry.
cards.gradeReason: Depression status from peering through — existential hit, but Depression needs a status system.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: broken glass watercolor. Subject: cracked window revealing tropical paradise from dim squalid room. Mood: paralyzing regret.

cards.power: Field Effect: Time flows in reverse. Winners become Losers.
cards.lore: Fun for the whole family, assuming the family hasn't been erased from existence.
cards.gradeReason: Time reversal, winners become losers — spectacular concept but mid-game reversal needs timing rules.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: spiral time watercolor. Subject: empty playground swingset in swirling vortex above spiral sandbox. Mood: temporal inversion.

cards.power: Chaos: Shuffle all discard piles into a new deck. Draw 5.
cards.lore: It hurts to exist.
cards.gradeReason: Chaos engine with maximum discard shuffle — needs discard pile loaded first to be spectacular.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: glitch pixel watercolor hybrid. Subject: robot-cat hybrid with smiley face and RGB glitch aura. Mood: joyful destruction.

cards.power: Delete: Physically tear up one card from an opponent's hand.
cards.lore: The only permanent cure for aging.
cards.gradeReason: Physically tear up an opponent's card — most visceral power in the game, zero ambiguity.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: erased ink on paper. Subject: giant pink eraser destroying card paper in close-up hand. Mood: permanent deletion.

cards.power: Bluff: Pretend you have a winning card. If no one calls you out, you win.
cards.lore: Value is subjective.
cards.gradeReason: Bluff a winning card — if nobody calls it, you win. Pure kayfabe at the table.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: IOU note illustration. Subject: IOU ONE FUTURE note pinned to corkboard with red pushpin. Mood: promissory audacity.

cards.power: Resign: Flip the table. Go outside. Play outside.
cards.lore: Game Over. You're still old. Go home.
cards.gradeReason: Flip the table, go outside — the only power that ends the game by ending the game.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: cartoon exit watercolor. Subject: FrizzleBob rabbit walking away waving BYE with ghost blob trailing behind. Mood: triumphant surrender.

verdict: The Wrinkle-Rumble Starter Kit is FrizzleBob firing on all cylinders — aging horror weaponized as card game, with mechanics that ARE the punchline. The multi-format structure (watercolor sketchbook, RAF slabs, scrapbook, clean bordered) functions as an intentional sampler of the whole Kayfabizarro aesthetic range. Weak spot: 'Future Timeline card' and 'Stolen Items' terminology appears across multiple cards but is never defined inside the deck itself. The Eraser's deliberately blurred LORE and The Blank Cheque's colored RAF boxes are chef's-kiss meta touches. Table-ready: YES.
blurb: For everyone who survived their own future. 48 cards of surreal aging comedy where time is a mechanic, identity is optional, and the only winning move is to flip the table.

coverQA.coverVisual: 5 — FrizzleBob dropkicking a melting Dali clock is compositionally perfect and instantly iconic
coverQA.coverTitle: 5 — 'Fractal Future Fantasy: The Wrinkle-Rumble Starter Kit' is sticky, absurd, and memorable
coverQA.coverVibeMatch: 5 — surreal time-decay comedy aesthetic nailed on first impression
coverQA.coverOriginality: 4 — strong but the melting-clock visual is well-trodden; the BLODSINN snail saves it
coverQA.coverViral: 5 — 'What the FLUFF?!' bird and exploding clock are both clip-worthy
coverQA.coverNote: Look, FrizzleBob karate-kicking a screaming clock is not subtle — it's a STATEMENT. The BLODSINN snail in the corner is the secret weapon: tiny, grumpy, holding a protest sign at a cartoon explosion. That snail is the deck in one image. Would not change it. Would frame it.

notes: Multi-format deck: four distinct card layouts across 13 pages — (1) 2x2 aged watercolor sketchbook [pp.2-7], (2) large-format RAF slab cards [p.8], (3) notebook/scrapbook-tape style [pp.9-10], (4) clean bordered cards [pp.11-13]. This variety functions as an intentional starter-kit sampler of all Kayfabizarro card aesthetics. RAF present on all cards. Foliage of Shame (card 4), Creaky-Knees Caliper (card 8), and Unsent Apology (card 12) show only [R][A] boxes without F-box — may be intentional 2-slot design. Font artifact: The 40th Grade of Desk (card 21) shows [A][A][F] rather than [R][A][F] — possible rendering artifact. The Eraser card (card 46) has its LORE section visually blurred/erased as a meta-joke. The Blank Cheque (card 47) features colored RAF boxes (R=red, A=orange, F=blue) — special formatting. Uncle FrizzleBob's Exit (card 48) has ghost/faded RAF boxes matching the exit theme. Wheelchair Joust (card 14) has power/lore positions deliberately inverted — flavor in POWER slot, mechanic in LORE slot. 'Future Timeline card' terminology referenced across at least 4 cards (Wrinkle-Storm, Denial Visor, Dream-Bubble Pop, Pearly Gatekeeper) but never defined within deck — needs glossary or rules companion.

urgent: Add 'Future Timeline card' definition — referenced in 4+ cards but undefined in this starter kit
quickWins: Verify F-box absence on Foliage of Shame, Creaky-Knees Caliper, Unsent Apology is intentional vs. print error
Add small visual indicator that The Eraser's blurred LORE is a meta-joke, not a print defect
niceToHave: 1-page glossary card for Starter Kit defining: Future, Stolen Items, Depression status, Dream Sequence
Consider adding Hover-Diaper's science-gravity line as standalone lore for clarity
Wheelchair Joust power/lore inversion is brilliant — add tiny asterisk so players know it's intentional

marketingText:
Kayfabizarro: Fractal Future Fantasy – The Wrinkle-Rumble Starter Kit (Free Cut & Play Comic Card Game)

Aging is the one opponent that never gets tired, never taps out, and always kicks out at two. So quit bracing for the slow decline. Climb through the ropes and wrestle it.

You were sold "graceful aging" as a product: the right serum, the right hat, the right tidy attitude, and the years stop hurting. That pitch is the con. The hat salesmen and the wellness merchants need you quiet, careful, and faintly ashamed of your own knees. Decay is coming either way. The only choice left is whether you meet it onstage with a microphone or in a waiting room holding a number ticket.

This is wrestling for the back half of your life. 48 cut-and-play cards where time is a mechanic, identity is optional, and the whole table performs the indignities out loud instead of whispering about them. Social Story Wrestling, geriatric division: you slam down a card, commit to the damage, and the room decides whether your collapse is tragic or hilarious. Usually both.

WHAT'S INSIDE?
- The Wrinkle-Rumble Core Deck: 48 High-Res "Print, Cut & Play" Cards, featuring The Cookie of Causality, the snickerdoodle that restarts the whole war from turn one, The Memory Lane Minefield, where every step detonates an old embarrassment, and Uncle FrizzleBob's Exit, the one card that wins by flipping the table and walking outside.
- The Freestyle Rules: the complete Anti-Rulebook. No complicated math, just storytelling, dice-driven chaos, and the RAF stat bar that lets the dice decide whether Repression, Acting-out, or Free-association carries the round.
- The Four-Format Sampler: one starter kit, four card looks. Aged watercolor sketchbook, big RAF slabs, taped-scrapbook pages, clean bordered cards. A guided tour of every Kayfabizarro aesthetic in a single box.

THE "LIVING DECK" PASS (Free Updates)
This deck is part of the Kayfabizarro main line. Grab it and you are not buying a frozen PDF, you are on the Protopian Pipeline: every future expansion and topic deck in this cycle reaches you as a free update, no second checkout.

WHY "PAY WHAT YOU WANT"?
I make these because the fastest way to pull the sting out of getting old is to perform it at a table full of people laughing with you. This deck is the warm-up I wanted for every birthday I dreaded. Are you broke? Enter "0" and take it. Print it, cut it, lose gracefully or flip the table. Want to support the craft? Every euro goes straight into the time I spend drawing the next cards.

Choose your reality. Become an Epistemic Outlaw.
"You never get to pin time. You only get to decide whether the crowd is laughing when it pins you."
Stay fluffy. — Uncle FrizzleBob
